publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: presupposition accommodation - the adjustment a conversation's common ground undergoes so that a sentence whose requirements it does not yet satisfy can still update it
span.quote: Presupposition accommodation is the process by which the context is ad- justed quietly and without fuss to accept the utterance of a sentence that imposes certain requirements on the context in which it is processed.

span.label: whether accommodation is mysterious, magical or needed, how hard it is, where it happens, and what exactly gets accommodated
span.quote: I will ask and attempt to answer the following questions: Is accommodation mysterious? Is it magic? Is it needed? How hard is it? Where does it happen? What gets accommodated?

span.label: defends the common-ground-plus-accommodation theory against the charges of magic and superfluity, and separates accommodation proper from two things routinely confused with it - grammatical presupposition cancellation, and reconstructing a conversation one is not a party to
span.quote: I argue that these complaints are mistaken: accommodation is not magic and is needed.

span.label: critique
span.quote: To be provocative, let me state that there is no local accommodation.

span.label: informative presupposition - a sentence presupposing something the hearer demonstrably does not yet believe, and succeeding anyway
span.quote: it is clear that this sentence can quite appropriately and successfully be uttered in a context where it is not already part of the common ground that the speaker has a daughter.

span.label: conceptual analysis in formal pragmatics: constructed example sentences judged for acceptability, and close reading of the rival definitions in the literature
span.term: conceptual analysis in formal pragmatics: constructed example sentences judged for acceptability, and close reading of the rival definitions in the literature
span.quote: I was commissioned to write a paper on accommodation as a semanticist.

span.label: an utterance changes the common ground in TWO steps - first the bare fact that it was made becomes common ground, and only then is the asserted proposition added; accommodation happens in the first step
span.quote: We see thus that an utterance will aﬀect the common ground in two steps: (i) ﬁrst, the fact that the utterance was made becomes common ground (and the participants may immediately draw inferences based on that fact, and perhaps adjust the common ground accordingly), (ii) then, assuming that the proper (implicit) negotiation has occurred, the asserted proposition is added to the common ground.

span.label: the prior context relevant to interpretation is the context AS CHANGED BY the fact that the speech act was made, which is why the pronoun I has a referent at all
span.quote: The prior context that is relevant to the interpretation of a speech act is the context as it is changed by the fact that the speech act was made, but prior to the acceptance or rejection of the speech act.

span.label: what makes the common ground adjustable is that it is constituted entirely by the participants' beliefs, and beliefs move in response to other people's actions
span.quote: What magic there is in accommodation lies in the fact that the common ground is an object that is constituted entirely by the beliefs of the partic- ipants in a conversation, and since people can change their beliefs at least to some extent in response to other people’s actions, the common ground is 8 Thony Gillies (pc) pointed out to me that accommodation can even occur when the hearer(s) antecedently believe the negation of the presupposition.

span.label: hearers do not weigh candidate PROPOSITIONS to add; they weigh candidate NEW COMMON GROUNDS by how plausibly the speaker intended them - which is what resolves the Proviso Problem
span.quote: What I propose is that we are not evaluating the plausibility of the candidate rescue propositions that might be added to the common ground, but we are evaluating candidates for the new common ground as to how plausible it is that the speaker intends the hearers to move to that new common ground to satisfy the presuppositions of the asserted sentence.

span.label: accommodation fails when the presupposition concerns a fact no mental adjustment can bring into being, such as what the conversation has actually made salient
span.quote: More generally, there cannot be accommodation with presuppositions that do not just target what is in the common ground but concern facts in the world that no manner of mental adjustment can bring into being.

span.label: a present-tense presupposition can be too early to accommodate: since we all know demands that the knowledge hold AT utterance time, which later accommodation cannot supply
span.quote: What is required is that at the time of utterance (because of the present tense), we all know that I have a daughter.

span.label: A DATED COINAGE WITH THE DEFINITION ATTACHED: `LEWIS IN HIS SCORE-KEEPING PAPER NAMED THE PHENOMENON “ACCOMMODATION”: The Rule of Accommodation for Presupposition - If at time t something is said that requires presupposition P to be acceptable, and if P is not presupposed just before t, then ... PRESUPPOSITION P COMES INTO EXISTENCE AT t. (Lewis 1979)` The naming act, the year, and the rule in one place.
span.quote: Lewis in his score-keeping paper named the phenomenon “accommodation”: The Rule of Accommodation for Presupposition If at time t something is said that requires presupposition P to be acceptable, and if P is not presupposed just before t, then — ceteris paribus and within certain limits — presupposition P comes into existence at t. (Lewis 1979)

span.label: AND THE TERM WAS BORN AS A SPECIAL CASE OF SOMETHING WIDER, WHICH IS WHY IT COULD TRAVEL: `For Lewis, presupposition accommodation was A SPECIAL CASE OF OTHER ADJUSTMENTS TO THE CONTEXT that are done quietly and without fuss when required.` A narrow technical term carved out of a general conversational phenomenon - and Thomason later takes it back to the general case.
span.quote: For Lewis, presupposition accommodation was a special case of other adjust- ments to the context that are done quietly and without fuss when required

span.label: A NAMED MISREADING OF A DEFINITION, QUOTED AND REBUTTED IN PRINT: `GAUKER (2008) MISUNDERSTANDS the proposal that presuppositions are preconditions that need to be satisfied before the common ground can be updated`, followed by Gauker's own words and then `THIS IS AN ERROR`. The corpus rarely catches one author telling another that he has the definition wrong, with both statements quoted.
span.quote: Gauker (2008) misun- derstands the proposal that presuppositions are preconditions that need to be satisﬁed before the common ground can be updated. He writes: “As we have seen, Heim understands a presupposition as a condition that a context must meet in order for a sentence to eﬀect an update. But what happens in real life if the condition is not met? Does the speaker’s utterance simply have no eﬀect whatsoever on the conversation? That just does not seem very realistic." This is an error

span.label: the paper cannot explain the very principle it relies on - why new information may be presupposed only when it is uncontroversial - and says so
span.quote: The problem is in explaining this principle: nothing in the framework we have in place derives the principle.

span.label: declared and left open: the author hands the challenge to future work rather than answering it here
span.quote: I will leave this a challenge for future work. 37

span.label: the account assumes hardwired semantic presuppositions and declines to defend that assumption against pragmatic-derivation approaches
span.quote: I am very skeptical that any such story can succeed, but will not argue the point here.3 So, I assume that there is a presuppositional component of meaning hardwired in the semantics of particular expressions.

span.label: it is agnostic about the semantic implementation, taking either a three-valued or a ccp-based wiring
span.quote: I am agnostic of the particular kind of wiring involved.

span.label: the analysis of the grammatical process it separates off is explicitly not given
span.quote: I will leave it open how exactly the grammatical process is to be analyzed: there are a number of proposals on the market, such as the syntactic manipulations in DRT approaches or the lexical insertion of an A-operator proposed by Beaver & Krahmer (2001).) To be provocative, let me state that there is no local accommodation.

span.label: the cases from Thomason of assuming leadership in a group and switching to the familiar pronoun, accommodation as a SOCIAL move imported to explain the conversational one
span.quote: Another familiar case, involving even more painful risks, is establishing intimacy, as in beginning to use a familiar pronoun to someone in a language like French or German.

span.label: the local and intermediate accommodation dispute is aligned with the embedded-implicature debate, and the same grammatical-versus-Gricean split is proposed for both
span.quote: As Beaver and Zeevat note, the topic of local/intermediate accommodation has considerable parallels to the ongoing debate about whether there are “em- bedded implicatures”.

span.label: the pretense account, on which the speaker merely acts as if the proposition is already common ground
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that informative presupposition needs no accommodation because nothing is really being presupposed · outcome: failed
span.quote: A] speaker may act as if certain propositions are part of the common background when he knows that they are not.

span.label: utterance presupposition, which relocates the requirement from the speaker to the utterance
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the problem dissolves by redefining who or what does the presupposing · outcome: failed
span.quote: An utterance U presupposes P (at t) iﬀone can reasonably infer from U that the speaker S accepts P and regards it as uncontroversial, either because a.

span.label: a set of candidate common grounds ordered by plausibility, as in Beaver 2001
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that uncertainty about the common ground, rather than adjustment of it, explains the data · outcome: partial
span.quote: He proposes a system where a participant’s model of a conversation is associated with a set of common ground candidates, ordered in terms of how plausible it is that a particular common ground candidate is in fact the common ground assumed or intended by the speaker.

span.label: the survey of alternatives to accommodation in Part 1 section 4
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that accommodation is superfluous because some other account does the same work · outcome: held
span.quote: In this section, we will go over some attempts to not use the process we explicated above.

span.label: common ground
span.quote: The common ground of a conversation at any given time is the set of propositions that the participants in that conversation at that time mutually assume to be taken for granted and not subject to (further) discussion.

span.label: context set
span.quote: The common ground describes a set of worlds, the context set, which are those worlds in which all of the propositions in the common ground are true.

span.label: accommodation
span.quote: But we need to admit into the picture a process by which the participants in a conversation quietly and without fuss adjust the common ground so as to satisfy the requirements of a sentence that was asserted by a participant in good standing.

span.label: Rule of Accommodation
span.quote: If at time t something is said that requires presupposition P to be acceptable, and if P is not presupposed just before t, then — ceteris paribus and within certain limits — presupposition P comes into existence at t.

span.label: local accommodation
span.quote: There is no local accommodation, just presupposition projection plus possible global accommodation of information about C.

span.label: intermediate accommodation
span.quote: Presuppositions of the nuclear scope are accommodated into the restricted term.

span.label: Utterance Presupposition
span.quote: An utterance U presupposes P (at t) iﬀone can reasonably infer from U that the speaker S accepts P and regards it as uncontroversial, either because a.

span.label: Proviso Problem
span.quote: Geurts calls this the “Proviso Problem”; his recommendation is to give up on theories of presupposition that predict these weak conditional presuppositions.

span.label: context change potential
span.quote: a semantics based directly on context-change potentials (ccps): sentences express partial functions from contexts to contexts, where the presuppositional component is given as the deﬁnedness condition that determines whether the ccp can be applied to a given context.

span.label: Common Ground Target
span.quote: Sentences asserted in a conversation are meant to update the common ground of that conversation.

span.label: pretense
span.quote: A] speaker may act as if certain propositions are part of the common background when he knows that they are not.

span.label: Informative Presuppositions
span.quote: Informative use of presupposition may be successful in two particular kinds of circumstances: (i) the listeners may be genuinely agnostic as to the truth of the relevant proposition, assume that the speaker knows about its truth, and trust the speaker not to speak inappropriately or falsely; (ii) the listeners may not want to challenge the speaker about the presupposed proposition, because it is irrelevant to their concerns and because the smoothness of the conversation is important enough to them to warrant a little leeway.8 So, no: accommodation is not mysterious.

span.label: common ground → context set
span.note: A FORMAL DEFINITION WITH NOTHING MEASURED, AND THE EIGHT-TYPE VOCABULARY HAS NO SLOT FOR IT. The context set IS the common ground stated extensionally - the paper restates one as the other in its own words. I tagged it `operationalised-as` and the gate refused: that type requires a MEASUREMENT OR DEFINITION cue, and it was right, because nothing here is measured. `same-as` is wrong too - a set of propositions and a set of worlds are different objects. What is needed is `defined-in-terms-of`, which does not exist. Dropped from concept_edges 2026-08-26 rather than forced into the nearest type.
span.quote: If this is a pragmatic presupposition of the sentence, then what is required is that the common ground include the proposition that someone broke the keyboard, in other words, that the con- text set only include worlds where someone broke the keyboard.

span.label: intermediate accommodation → local accommodation
span.note: A RENAMING INSIDE ONE FIELD, AND THE ONLY SENTENCE THAT STATES IT IS DAMAGED. The paper says the process `was sometimes called “local accommodation” but is now more usually termed “intermediate accommodation”` - and the staged text carries the page number 30 wedged inside the phrase, `termed “intermediate 30 accommodation”`. Quoted as an edge label that would read as a tagging error forever. `renamed-across-fields` is also the wrong type: this is one field renaming its own term, not a name crossing between fields. Evidence here is Berman's formulation instead, which states the process without naming it. A DAMAGED SENTENCE IS NOT THE ONLY SENTENCE - except when it is the only one that says the thing, and then the relation goes here.
span.quote: Presuppositions of the nuclear scope are accommodated into the restricted term.

span.label: accommodation - Lewis's rule, where the presupposition COMES INTO EXISTENCE on demand and the process therefore looks like magic
span.quote: Lewis’ formulation indeed makes accommodation seem rather magical.

span.label: accommodation - the timing account, where nothing appears from nowhere because the requirement falls due at UPDATE time, not before the utterance
span.quote: Thus, the common ground must satisfy the presuppositional requirements before the update can be performed, not actually before the utterance occurs.

span.label: accommodation - Thomason's SOCIAL sense, the same move by which a person assumes authority or intimacy by acting as if they already had it
span.quote: But people can be accommodating, and in fact there are many social situations in which the best way to get what we want is to act as if we already had it.

span.label: `presupposition` (Stalnaker's own usage) - AND HE SAYS HIS OWN DEFINITION DOES NOT COVER IT: under pretense `the speaker's presuppositions, IN THE SENSE OF THE TERM I SHALL USE, WILL NOT FIT THE DEFINITION SKETCHED ABOVE ... THAT IS WHY THE DEFINITION IS ONLY AN APPROXIMATION.` An author stipulating a usage that exceeds the definition he has just given, and labelling the definition an approximation rather than repairing it.
span.quote: Where a conversation involves this kind of pretense, the speaker’s presuppositions, in the sense of the term I shall use, will not ﬁt the deﬁnition sketched above [to presuppose something is to assume that it is mutually assumed to be true]. That is why the deﬁnition is only an approximation

span.label: contradicts → Burton-Roberts (1989) and Gauker (1998), that informative presuppositions are fatal to the common ground theory
span.quote: Some people, including Burton-Roberts (1989) and Gauker (1998), have thought that this is indeed a fatal problem for the common ground theory.

span.label: critiques → Soames (1982), that informative presuppositions undermine every definition requiring the presupposed proposition to be present before the utterance
span.quote: But note that this in fact is not what the common ground theory of presupposition says, at least not once we look very closely at what it tries to do.

span.label: builds-on → Stalnaker (1998) on the time-dependence of context
span.quote: This perspective on the time-dependent nature of presuppositional as- sumptions is made clear by Stalnaker in his more recent work on context dynamics (Stalnaker 1998), emphases added by me:

span.label: critiques → the definitional repair by Soames via utterance presupposition
span.quote: It is left open why one would be able to reasonably that infer that the speaker thinks that the audience is prepared to add the presupposed proposition P, without objection, to the context against which U is evaluated.

span.label: critiques → Beaver (2001), that a set of candidate common grounds handles informative presupposition
span.quote: On the confused view, the candidate common grounds are those that for all it is known might be the actual common ground.

span.label: contradicts → Berman (1991), that nuclear-scope presuppositions are accommodated into the restrictor
span.quote: Beaver (2004) and I argue that there is no such process.

span.label: contradicts → Geurts (1996), that the Proviso Problem should be solved by abandoning weak conditional presuppositions
span.quote: his recommendation is to give up on theories of presupposition that predict these weak conditional presuppositions.

span.label: local accommodation —distinct-from→ accommodation
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — the sharpest claim in the paper - the two share a name and not a mechanism
span.quote: So, the kind of “local accommodation” appealed to here is not really the same kind of accommodation that we have discussed before.

span.label: pretense —contrasted-with→ accommodation
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.85
span.quote: Presupposing is thus not a mental attitude like believing, but it is rather a linguistic disposition — a disposition to behave in one’s use of language as if one had certain beliefs, or were making certain assumptions.

span.label: accommodation is not mysterious once the presupposition is understood as falling due at update time rather than before the utterance
span.quote: So, no: accommodation is not mysterious.

span.label: there is no local accommodation; what is called that is either a grammatical process or global accommodation about the quantifier domain
span.quote: There is no local accommodation, just presupposition projection plus possible global accommodation of information about C.

span.label: no alternative to the common ground plus accommodation picture survived examination
span.quote: In conclusion: we have seen no viable alternative to the common ground + accommodation view explicated earlier.

span.label: what gets accommodated is fixed by the best guess of the hearers at the intended new common ground, not by minimality
span.quote: So, what gets accommodated depends on the best guess of the hear- ers about what the speaker might have intended as the adjustment to the common ground that would admit the asserted sentence.21 Conclusion I have argued that accommodation is a natural component of the dynamics of discourse.

span.label: the stronger unconditional proposition cannot be accommodated for being more plausible, because it asymmetrically entails the weaker conditional one
span.quote: So, it cannot possibly be more plausible that Theo has a wife than that he has a wife if he hates sonnets.20 What probably 20 If one thinks about this at the level of the context set (the set of worlds compatible with the common ground), the options seem to be to remove from the context set all worlds where Theo doesn’t have a wife or merely all the ones where he hates sonnets but doesn’t have a wife.

span.label: pragmatic presupposition as a requirement imposed on the common ground
span.quote: Sentences can have pragmatic presuppositions in the sense of imposing certain requirements on the common ground.

span.label: the bridge principle licensing a partial proposition to update a body of information
span.quote: Partial or three-valued propositions can only be used to update a body of information if all worlds compatible with that body of information are such that the proposition gives a (non-stigmatized) truth-value to them.

span.label: taking a proposition to be uncontroversial, the substitute offered for speaker presupposition
span.quote: A speaker S takes a proposition P to be uncontroversial at t (or, equiv- 19 alently, takes P for granted at t) iﬀat t, S accepts P and thinks a. that P is already part of the conversational context at t; or b. that the other members of the conversation are prepared to add P to the context without objection.

span.label: the rule of accommodation as originally stated by Lewis
span.quote: If at time t something is said that requires presupposition P to be acceptable, and if P is not presupposed just before t, then — ceteris paribus and within certain limits — presupposition P comes into existence at t.

span.label: the free domain-restriction variable C on a quantifier, presupposed to be familiar
span.quote: There is a familiarity presupposition associated with the C variable.
